CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2 The Protection of Women and Children is implemented based on the principles of: a. respect and fulfillment of the rights of victims; b. justice; c. non-discrimination; d. best interests of victims; e. legal certainty; and f. legal protection.
Article 13 The Protection of Women and Children aims to: a. prevent all forms of violence against Women and Children; b. protect women and children; and c. provide services to Women and Children victims of violence.

CHAPTER IV OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 5
(1) The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility in providing Protection to Women and Children.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. implementing the obligations of Protection of Women and Children based on laws and regulations; b. establishing policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children; c. completing facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; d. allocating budget in the implementation of Protection of Women and Children; and e. fostering and supervising the implementation of Protection of Women and Children.
Article 6
(1) The community has the obligation and responsibility in providing Protection to Women and Children.
(2) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are implemented in the form of; a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against Women and Children; b. providing Protection to victims; c. providing emergency assistance; d. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against Women and Children to the competent authorities; and e. participating in the handling of victims of violence.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Tabalong Regency.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head, hereinafter referred to as the Regent, is the Regent of Tabalong.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tabalong Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tabalong Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-based violence is any act caused by an imbalance of power in the relations between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women and children either physically, sexually and/or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion, or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, occurring in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
11. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including the fetus in the womb.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Activity Center that provides services for women and children victims of violence in Tabalong Regency free of charge, covering information services, psychological consultation, legal consultation and religious consultation, assistance and advocacy, as well as health services and a safe house with referrals.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Article 4 Every Woman and Child has the right: a. to have their dignity and worth as human beings respected; b. to obtain protection from family, community, Regional Government and/or other parties either temporarily or based on the determination of a protection order from the court; c. to restoration of physical, psychological and sexual health in accordance with the suffering experienced by the victim; d. to special handling related to the confidentiality of the victim; e. to assistance by social workers and legal aid at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; f. to spiritual guidance services; and g. to determine their own decisions.

CHAPTER VI MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 11
(1) To guarantee synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence in the Region.
(3) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations that implement policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.
(4) Monitoring is conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the current year.
Article 12
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER X COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 17 (1) In implementing Protection for Women and Children, the community may: a. form family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community; b. conduct socialization of the rights of Women and Children independently; c. provide first aid to victims; and d. report to the competent authority if violence against Women and Children occurs in the environment.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector and mass media.

Article 10
In providing Protection to Women and Children, P2TP2A is obligated to: a. provide services as quickly as possible and free of charge to victims; b. organize protection and fulfillment of victims' rights to Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance; c. cooperate with certain institutions in providing translators and volunteer assistants needed for victims; d. provide convenience, comfort and safety for victims; and e. maintain the confidentiality of victims.

CHAPTER IX GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children in the Region.
Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, facilitation, guidance, supervision, consultation, education and training.
Article 16
In the context of supervision, the Regent conducts monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.

Article 14 Financing for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children is sourced from the regional revenue and expenditure budget and other sources that are legal and non-binding.

CHAPTER VII REPORTING
Article 13
(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing reports on the implementation of P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children in the Region.
(2) Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually or when necessary and submitted to the Provincial Government.
(3) The form of report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

1.8.rationale: The original regulation does not define or include human trafficking as a form/scope of violence in its operative provisions; it mainly defines gender-based violence as physical/sexual/psychological harm (Pasal 1 angka 8) and regulates protection services via P2TP2A. The only trafficking-related content is in the legal basis list ("Mengingat"), which cites UU No. 21 Tahun 2007 tentang Pemberantasan Tindak Pidana Perdagangan Orang. Citing a national law in the preamble does not, by itself, mean the local regulation’s scope explicitly covers trafficking as an indicator. The judge treated the legal-basis citation as substantive inclusion, which is an overreach given the document’s actual definitions and service provisions.

2.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text includes "rekam kasus" as a step in the P2TP2A handling flow (Pasal 9 ayat (1) huruf g) and requires annual reporting by the Bupati on P2TP2A implementation (Pasal 13). However, the indicator "Data collection systems" typically implies a broader, formalized data system (e.g., mandated data collection framework, database/system, standardized indicators, aggregation across agencies). The cited provisions are about case file recording within a service workflow and administrative reporting, not an explicit data collection system. The judge inferred a full data-collection system from minimal recordkeeping/reporting language, so the "Yes" is too lenient relative to what the regulation actually specifies.

2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head, hereinafter referred to as the Regent, is the Regent of Tabalong.
4. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Agency is the Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tabalong Regency.
6. Head of Agency is the Head of the Agency for Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning of Tabalong Regency.
7. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
8. Gender-based violence is any act caused by an imbalance of power in the relations between women and men that results in misery or suffering of women and children either physically, sexually and/or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion, or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, occurring in the private/domestic sphere and in the public sphere.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Woman is an adult human of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
11. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including the fetus in the womb.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence.
13. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter referred to as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Activity Center that provides services for women and children victims of violence in Tabalong Regency free of charge, covering information services, psychological consultation, legal consultation and religious consultation, assistance and advocacy, as well as health services and a safe house with referrals.

CHAPTER VI MONITORING AND EVALUATION
Article 11
(1) To guarantee synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for the Protection of Women and Children victims of violence in the Region.
(3) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus Organizations that implement policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.
(4) Monitoring is conducted starting from planning through the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the current year.
Article 12
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children is conducted at the end of each fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 15
(1) The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision over the implementation of P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children in the Region.
Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, facilitation, guidance, supervision, consultation, education and training.
Article 16
In the context of supervision, the Regent conducts monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.

Article 10
In providing Protection to Women and Children, P2TP2A is obligated to: a. provide services as quickly as possible and free of charge to victims; b. organize protection and fulfillment of victims' rights to Health Rehabilitation, Social Rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance; c. cooperate with certain institutions in providing translators and volunteer assistants needed for victims; d. provide convenience, comfort and safety for victims; and e. maintain the confidentiality of victims.

CHAPTER III RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
Article 4 Every Woman and Child has the right: a. to have their dignity and worth as human beings respected; b. to obtain protection from family, community, Regional Government and/or other parties either temporarily or based on the determination of a protection order from the court; c. to restoration of physical, psychological and sexual health in accordance with the suffering experienced by the victim; d. to special handling related to the confidentiality of the victim; e. to assistance by social workers and legal aid at every level of the examination process in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; f. to spiritual guidance services; and g. to determine their own decisions.

CHAPTER VII REPORTING
Article 13
(1) The Regent is responsible for preparing reports on the implementation of P2TP2A for the Protection of Women and Children in the Region.
(2) Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be conducted annually or when necessary and submitted to the Provincial Government.
(3) The form of report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER VIII FINANCING
Article 14 Financing for the implementation of the Protection of Women and Children is sourced from the regional revenue and expenditure budget and other sources that are legal and non-binding.

"Sosialisasi" in Indonesian policy context is an information/education/awareness-raising activity. This is directly relevant to information/education as primary prevention.
